theory.intro: The three interior angles of any triangle add to $180^{\circ}$. Drawing a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side shows why. Knowing two angles then gives the third.
facts: The interior angle sum of a triangle is $180^{\circ}$: $a+b+c=180^{\circ}$.
Alternate angles on the parallel lines give $\angle DBA=\angle BAC$ and $\angle EBC=\angle BCA$.
The three angles at $B$ lie on the straight line $DBE$, so they add to $180^{\circ}$, and so do the angles of the triangle.
The two base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, so the equation becomes $2a+b=180^{\circ}$.
A right angle uses $90^{\circ}$ of the sum, so the other two angles of a right-angled triangle add to $90^{\circ}$.
When angles are given as expressions, add the expressions, set the total equal to $180$ and solve.
steps: Write an equation using the angle sum.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The interior angles of a triangle total $180^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}a+58+38&=180\\a+96&=180\\a&=84\end{align*}$

The missing angle is $84^{\circ}$.

The square marks a $90^{\circ}$ angle.

$\begin{align*}a+35+90&=180\\a+125&=180\\a&=55\end{align*}$

The missing angle is $55^{\circ}$.

Equal sides have equal opposite angles, so both base angles are $58^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}a+58+58&=180\\a+116&=180\\a&=64\end{align*}$

The missing angle is $64^{\circ}$.

The two base angles are equal; each is $a^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}a+a+104&=180\\2a+104&=180\\2a&=76\\a&=38\end{align*}$

The missing angle is $38^{\circ}$.

workedExamples.question_text: One angle in an isosceles triangle is $72^{\circ}$. Find both possible pairs of other angles and explain why there are two answers.
workedExamples.solution_text:
If $72^{\circ}$ is the angle between the equal sides, let each base angle be $a^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}2a+72&=180\\2a&=108\\a&=54\end{align*}$

The other angles are $54^{\circ}$ and $54^{\circ}$.

If $72^{\circ}$ is a base angle, the other base angle is also $72^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}a+72+72&=180\\a+144&=180\\a&=36\end{align*}$

The other angles are $72^{\circ}$ and $36^{\circ}$. Both cases are possible because the given angle's position is unspecified.

workedExamples.question_text: One angle in an isosceles triangle is $152^{\circ}$. Find the other two angles and explain why there is only one possible pair.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The given angle cannot be a base angle: two angles of $152^{\circ}$ would total $304^{\circ}$, exceeding $180^{\circ}$. It is the angle between the equal sides.

Let each base angle be $a^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}2a+152&=180\\2a&=28\\a&=14\end{align*}$

The other angles are $14^{\circ}$ and $14^{\circ}$.

workedExamples.question_text: Use algebra to explain why every angle in an equilateral triangle is $60^{\circ}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
All three angles are equal. Let each angle be $a^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}a+a+a&=180\\3a&=180\\a&=60\end{align*}$

Every angle is $60^{\circ}$.

workedExamples.question_text: An isosceles triangle has an interior angle of $60^{\circ}$. Find the other angles and explain what this tells you about the triangle.
workedExamples.solution_text:
If the given angle is between the equal sides, let each base angle be $a^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}2a+60&=180\\2a&=120\\a&=60\end{align*}$

If the given angle is a base angle, the other base angle is also $60^{\circ}$.

$\begin{align*}a+60+60&=180\\a+120&=180\\a&=60\end{align*}$

Both cases give three angles of $60^{\circ}$, so the triangle is equilateral.

development.question_text:
One of the angles in an isosceles triangle is $76^{\circ}$.
Find the sizes of the other two angles, and explain why there is more than one possible answer.
development.solution_text:
If $76^{\circ}$ is the angle between the two equal sides:
$2x+76=180$
$2x=104$
$x=52^{\circ}$, so the other two angles are $52^{\circ}$ and $52^{\circ}$.
If $76^{\circ}$ is one of the two equal angles:
$x+76+76=180$
$x=28^{\circ}$, so the other two angles are $76^{\circ}$ and $28^{\circ}$.
The question does not say whether $76^{\circ}$ is one of the equal angles, so both are possible.

Use algebra to explain why every angle in an equilateral triangle is $60^{\circ}$.
development.solution_text:
Let each of the three equal angles be $x^{\circ}$.
$x+x+x=180$
$3x=180$
$x=60$, so every angle of an equilateral triangle is $60^{\circ}$.

mastery.question_text:
An isosceles triangle has an interior angle of $60^{\circ}$.
Find the other two angles, and state what this tells you about the triangle.
mastery.solution_text:
If $60^{\circ}$ is the angle between the two equal sides:
$2x+60=180$
$x=60^{\circ}$
If $60^{\circ}$ is one of the two equal angles:
$x+60+60=180$
$x=60^{\circ}$
Both cases give three angles of $60^{\circ}$, so an isosceles triangle containing a $60^{\circ}$ angle must be equilateral.
